yuan2026improving: Guidance for diffusion models extrapolates between main and inferior signals, but when to use classifier-free versus automatic guidance was unclear. Synthetic analysis frames both as weak-to-strong extrapolation methods and maps their effective regimes. Segmented Guidance hybridizes them at inference, and the same weak-to-strong principle is also migrated into the training objective so unguided models generalize better. On SD3 and SD3.5 it beats existing training-free guidance, and transformer training-time experiments show gains in conditional and unconditional settings.
yuan2026videostar: Open-vocabulary action recognition is hard because text-centric priors cannot separate semantically similar actions. Video-STAR decomposes actions into discriminative sub-motions for fine-grained matching and dynamically calls tools such as pose estimation and human detection to interleave cross-modal reasoning. A hierarchical reward balancing tool use, sub-motion relevance, and coherence trains the model by reinforcement learning without explicit supervision. On HMDB-51, UCF-101, SSv2, Kinetics-400, and Kinetics-600 it reaches state-of-the-art, reducing cross-modal hallucination in fine-grained action recognition.
zhai2025peripheral: Long-term knowledge updates in LLMs remain hard without retraining. The work treats memory as peripheral RAM beside the LLM as CPU: a sequence of memory banks modeled with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks enables smooth state transitions, and read-write operations are gated by query signals derived from the model's internal states. A sign-bit-like relevance bank masks retrieved memory, which is injected as a prefix. On knowledge-editing benchmarks the peripheral memory is effective and efficient for integrating new information.
zhang2026vdeal: Video LLMs fail safety in a counterintuitive way: harmful videos paired with benign queries are attacked more often than harmful videos paired with explicit harmful queries. V-DEAL diagnoses this across behavior, understanding, and internal representations on six video LLMs and three benchmarks: models recognize harmful content over 81 percent of the time yet still leak details under benign prompts at a 48.33 percent attack success rate, and hidden-state analysis shows visual content activates weaker refusal than text. A prompt-injection intervention cuts attack success by 48.24 points, matching fine-tuning-based defenses.
zhao2019optimization: Estimating a combinatorial graph Laplacian under a known topology is a non-convex problem. Two optimization schemes, ADMM and majorization-minimization, yield GLE-ADMM and GLE-MM, both reaching an optimality gap of 1e-4, about three orders better than the prior benchmark. ADMM suits dense near-complete graphs while MM suits sparse trees, and a third algorithm, GLENE, seeds the problem with leading eigenvectors of the sample covariance as a nominal subspace. The subspace initialization helps most when the sample size is small relative to dimension.
zhong2025mquake: Multi-hop knowledge editing relies on MQuAKE, but an audit finds up to 33 percent of its questions and 76 percent of ground-truth labels are corrupted by clerical errors. MQuAKE-Remastered repairs the dataset without shrinking it and re-benchmarks published editing methods, revealing that many overfit original MQuAKE's quirks rather than improve real multi-hop editing. The audit and fixed dataset establish a more reliable evaluation and a guideline for honest benchmark use in knowledge editing.
zhu2025mitigating: Multi-hop RAG loses key entities during sub-question decomposition, which breaks retrieval and the reasoning chain. ChainRAG handles sub-questions sequentially: each step completes missing entities and retrieves relevant sentences from a sentence graph, building on prior answers, before integrating all retrieved evidence into the final answer. On MuSiQue, 2Wiki, and HotpotQA with GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-72B, and GLM-4-Plus, it beats baselines in both accuracy and efficiency.
zhu2026save: Reasoning models overthink even when prompted to stop, especially on hard questions. Analysis across termination confidence, attention distributions, and attention allocation finds high perplexity predicts continued thinking, and still-thinking cases attend more to the original question. An attention intervention that forces the no-thinking mode suppresses deliberation but also lowers accuracy, showing the suppressed reasoning is genuinely useful. The result quantifies the trade-off between instruction following, inference cost, and correctness.
